question.text: Ramesh wants to accumulate Rs.2 crore for retirement in 30 years. If he earns 10% annual return on investments, approximately how much must he invest per month?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook uses exactly this Rs.2 crore, 30-year, 10% example to contrast idle saving with investing. Saving idle requires roughly Rs.55,555 per month (Rs.2 crore divided by 360 months), but investing at a 10% return reduces the required monthly contribution to about Rs.8,847 because of the compounding of returns over the 30-year horizon. The Trap: Rs.55,555 is the idle-savings number — the figure the workbook deliberately contrasts with the invested figure to make the point about compounding. Rs.15,000 and Rs.25,000 are mid-range distractors that ignore the assumed return rate altogether. Note: The workbook also illustrates the cost of delay using its own numbers — for example, a 5-year delay can lift a required monthly contribution from Rs.6,700 to Rs.10,500, and a 10-year delay can roughly double the required monthly contribution. Quote the workbook's own delay figures rather than generalising them.
